lxc_2435f66283cbda05.text: Astronomers have never visited an exoplanet, yet they can measure its size, mass, and even guess what its surface is made of.

lxc_11de5410e3efd442.text: A rocky world called 55 Cancri e became famous when scientists proposed it might be covered in carbon minerals — possibly diamond.

lxc_7bd2e38044d66ae7.text: Follow the evidence chain that made that claim possible, and see how one new measurement can change everything.

lxc_77666309a96dbe82.text: Exoplanets orbit stars dozens or hundreds of light-years away.

lxc_3ad33877d39aecc0.text: No spacecraft will reach them in a human lifetime, so every measurement is indirect.

lxc_b6546d144b66f808.text: Two techniques do most of the work.

lxc_02224d10781992e3.text: The transit method watches a star's brightness.

lxc_20f4a755e81045e2.text: When a planet crosses in front of its star, it blocks a tiny fraction of the light — sometimes less than one percent.

lxc_0ba5fa9e592ee011.text: By measuring how much the brightness drops and how often it repeats, astronomers calculate the planet's diameter and orbital period.

lxc_4250dec9dd777dbe.text: NASA's Kepler mission used this method to confirm thousands of exoplanets, including 55 Cancri e, which orbits its star in just under 18 hours.

lxc_725f945d817b9005.text: The radial velocity method listens to a star's motion.

lxc_1165583f68be499e.text: A planet's gravity tugs the star slightly toward and away from Earth as it orbits, shifting the star's light toward the red or blue end of the spectrum — the Doppler effect.

lxc_645474025098a63e.text: The size of that shift reveals the planet's minimum mass.

lxc_feaa61eb06b3c30b.text: Combining a transit radius with a radial velocity mass gives density: the single number that tells scientists whether a world is likely to be rocky, icy, or gassy.

lxc_4721171bd1b22459.text: Light carries atmospheric clues, but scientists must separate each measurement from the explanations that might fit it.

lxc_8b2e7a37e4b8ea28.text: Once scientists know a planet's size and mass, they turn to light for chemical clues.

lxc_2d282b1718c8dfca.text: Two approaches reveal what is in or around a planet.

lxc_216393886333bcca.text: Transit spectroscopy splits the starlight that passes through a planet's atmosphere into its spectrum.

lxc_c406d71488072637.text: Different gases absorb specific wavelengths, leaving dark lines — absorption features — like a chemical fingerprint.

lxc_8e1e452d66aece93.text: This is how astronomers have detected water vapour, methane, and carbon dioxide in the atmospheres of gas giants.

lxc_95f41ce1e97c700a.text: Secondary eclipse photometry measures what happens when a planet moves behind its star.

lxc_69274e94797f67cb.text: Just before disappearance, the telescope records light from both star and planet together; when the planet is hidden, it records only the star.

lxc_b57c544b8921f098.text: The difference is the planet's own thermal emission — its heat glow.

lxc_4684804ad9c08327.text: In 2024, the James Webb Space Telescope used secondary-eclipse observations of 55 Cancri e and found the planet's dayside is hotter than a bare rock should be.

lxc_60209d69f2381040.text: One explanation that fits the data is that heat is being redistributed by a thin atmosphere of carbon dioxide or carbon monoxide.

lxc_15279aca4f3f9db2.text: The team described this as a hint rather than a confirmation, because other explanations — such as a magma ocean releasing volcanic gases — are also consistent with the measurements.

lxc_44ffafd0996bb629.text: In 2012, researchers published a striking possible explanation for 55 Cancri e.

lxc_b30a87305fb5f78d.text: They used the planet's measured mass and radius to test different descriptions of its interior.

lxc_a45d00c54809d87b.text: One model assumed that the planet had much more carbon than Earth.

lxc_773434d4cddeff2c.text: Under the enormous pressure and heat inside a super-Earth, that composition could include a graphite layer and diamond deeper down.

lxc_277e4df56e9a81ec.text: The model depended on an important input: the carbon-to-oxygen ratio, or C/O ratio, of the host star.

lxc_a54860c859642cd8.text: Rocky planets form from material around young stars, so the star's chemistry can give clues about the material available when a planet formed.

lxc_f8841bcf19a24437.text: Early measurements suggested that 55 Cancri had a high C/O ratio, which made a carbon-rich planet seem possible.

lxc_ee165f7abc0b22ec.text: The paper did not report a direct detection of diamond.

lxc_fa8f11774754d246.text: It showed that a carbon-rich interior was one hypothesis consistent with the mass, radius, and stellar data available at the time.

lxc_98c8449523723118.text: The memorable phrase "diamond planet" made that careful possibility sound more certain than it was.

lxc_749a7afdc2197437.text: It helps to separate three levels of a scientific claim.

lxc_b29038622b846445.text: A direct measurement is something an instrument records, such as a change in starlight, an orbital time, or infrared brightness.

lxc_e85315061acf09b0.text: An inference connects measurements with physical laws: mass and radius, for example, allow scientists to infer density.

lxc_cde21f15b8d54b12.text: A hypothesis or model is a possible explanation that still needs testing.

lxc_5e76f3e7f07331b8.text: An interior model, for example, can describe a possible carbon-rich planet.

lxc_844f43a2a08200df.text: Models also need reliable rules about matter.

lxc_93a1eb6ed1d617b6.text: In laboratory experiments, researchers study small samples under very high pressure and temperature, or measure how gases interact with different wavelengths of light.

lxc_bdb039aba5b19e5a.text: These tests show how materials can change and what signals they may produce.

lxc_817c13f9a8d10d83.text: Computer models use those results and established physics to calculate which layers and materials could match a planet's measured mass, radius, temperature, and spectrum.

lxc_f76a75fc9a88cfd8.text: Researchers then compare each model's predictions with new observations.

lxc_ccf5bbb4e056bc1e.text: Several interiors can sometimes produce the same average density, so a model that fits the data remains possible rather than proven.

lxc_46a50c75638cc10f.text: A new measurement may rule one model out or make another more likely.

lxc_381bddc8539d6eb4.text: A scientific model is therefore a useful, testable picture — not a photograph of a place scientists have never visited.

lxc_58fb6d8dbbfe5e0a.text: Uncertainty is part of the evidence, and revision is the normal response when better measurements arrive.

lxc_408754c5d37b85ce.text: Science is not a fixed answer but a process of revision.

lxc_349c30f900d7988a.text: A later analysis of the stellar spectrum of 55 Cancri using improved methods found a significantly lower carbon-to-oxygen ratio than the 2012 study had assumed.

lxc_6d8e7abf246ba988.text: With a more Earth-like C/O ratio, the extreme carbon-rich interior model becomes much less likely.

lxc_7ccf84c6390e8817.text: The planet's mass and radius still allow a rocky composition, but a diamond-and-graphite mantle is no longer the most probable reading of the evidence.

lxc_30f7769ba7498be0.text: This revision did not mean the original researchers made an error.

lxc_646b220865ba5e8c.text: They used the best stellar data available in 2012.

lxc_392f8dd7af91f3b8.text: The later study applied refined spectroscopic techniques and a different model atmosphere for the star itself, producing a more precise abundance measurement.

lxc_3120787baee8986f.text: The change illustrates how a model is only as reliable as its inputs: improve the stellar measurement, and the planetary inference changes with it.

lxc_8f1cefeaad68e601.text: The 2024 Webb results add a further layer.

lxc_321dd763c90aee23.text: An atmosphere hints at ongoing geological activity — possibly a magma ocean — which itself constrains interior conditions.

lxc_5e478bf15a05567b.text: Each new observation narrows the range of plausible models without yet producing a single definitive answer.
